name: linear-search
description: Same kind of linear problem, smaller (200 actions in R^10, 5 instances, 4 runs each). LinUCB and LinTS with theoretical values, then with the best alpha and lambda found on other seeds.

notes: lambda_=0.1 (any lambda > 0 keeps the bound valid)

notes: lambda_=0.1 (any lambda > 0 keeps the bound valid)

policies.label: LinTS searched
notes: lambda_=0.1 (any lambda > 0 keeps the bound valid)

notices.title: Default hyperparameters
notices.text: Values of the papers: LinUCB alpha=1, LinTS alpha=1. They give the theoretical confidence bounds: safe in theory, but they often explore too much in practice. To fit them to this problem, run a grid search (param_grid=True, or "param_grid": true in a config file) or set them, e.g. LinUCB(alpha=0.1).

notices.title: Grid search
notices.text: LinUCB searched and LinTS searched: 18 combinations run 2 time(s) per instance before the reported runs (criterion: final regret). The values found fit this problem only: report them as such.

notices.title: Not stored
notices.text: Pseudo-regret (track "pseudo_regret"); action of every step (track "actions"); peak memory (measure_memory=True). The dashboard and the figures cannot show what is not stored; the brackets say how to store it (in a config file: "track": [...] or "measure_memory": true in "experiment").

notices.title: One point every 10 steps
notices.text: Curves keep one point every 10 steps and the last step (log_interval=10). The values at these points are exact. Between two points, the charts draw a straight line: there the curve is interpolated, not measured. log_interval=1 keeps every step (larger files).

notices.title: Parallel runs
notices.text: With n_jobs=4, each process uses one BLAS thread: compare CPU times only between runs with the same n_jobs.
